title: Metric Signal Synchronizer for LLM Inference
creator: Anika Shah
description: Build a tenant-scoped signal synchronizer that accepts Prometheus scrapes and OTLP metric streams from inference nodes, normalizes labels and metric names, deduplicates overlapping payloads, and emits a single canonical stream to downstream SLO and billing pipelines. The synchronizer must preserve high-cardinality labels for per-tenant attribution while enabling controlled rollups for long-term storage and SLO computation.
background: Current setup ingests Prometheus scrapes directly into the aggregator and receives OTLP metrics from edge sidecars. This has led to duplicate events (scrape + OTLP), inconsistent label schemas across language runtimes, and noisy cardinality growth when tenants attach custom request metadata. Multiple downstream consumers (SLO engine, billing, observability dashboards) require slightly different views of the same base signal. We need a single service to act as the canonical normalization and routing point.
technical_design: The synchronizer will run as a horizontally scalable stateless ingress with a short-lived local cache for dedupe and fast label canonicalization. Inputs: Prometheus remote_write, OTLP/gRPC metrics, and a small HTTP JSON shim for legacy agents. Key responsibilities: 1) schema normalization using a configurable mapping (eg. 'model_id' | 'model' | 'model_name' -> 'model'), 2) tenant resolution from token header or mTLS cert, 3) deduplication using time-windowed fingerprinting keyed by tenant+request_id+metric_family, 4) cardinality control via a policy that marks dimensions as low/medium/high and applies sampling or hash-binning for high-cardinality tokens, 5) multi-output fanout: canonical OTLP for SLO engine, Prometheus remote_write-compatible stream for Prom-archiver, and a compact cost-attribution report for billing. The config will be stored in a central config-service and hot-reloaded. Metrics will be emitted for dropped-label counts, dedupe rates, canonicalization errors, and per-tenant throughput.
tradeoffs:
- Stateful vs stateless dedupe: we choose short-lived local cache to keep the service horizontally scalable and avoid external DB latency. This may miss duplicates that cross instance boundaries but reduces operational complexity.
- Preserve vs collapse labels: default preserves label keys, with tenant policy allowing controlled collapse to limit cardinality.
- Single service vs sidecar: centralizes logic for easier policy rollout but increases blast radius; we'll mitigate with strict rate limits and circuit breakers.
acceptance_criteria: The synchronizer accepts Prometheus remote_write and OTLP/gRPC concurrently and exposes a /health and /metrics endpoint.
Duplicate events (scrape + OTLP for same request_id) are deduplicated in 95%+ of test scenarios within a 30s window.
Canonicalization rules map at least 90% of known variant keys (model, model_id, model_name) without manual intervention.
Per-tenant throughput of 10k metrics/sec sustained per instance without OOM on a 4CPU/8GB node (benchmark run attached).
Fanout outputs exist for: SLO OTLP stream, Prometheus remote_write for long-term archiver, and billing report; consumers can subscribe via Kafka topic or HTTP webhook.
Automated tests that simulate mixed OTLP + Prometheus inputs, high-cardinality tenant metadata, and failure scenarios are present in the repo and pass in CI.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) Deploy to a shadow namespace ingesting 10% of traffic (shadow compares outputs with current path), 2) Run parity checks for 72 hours and fix mismatches, 3) Enable fanout for billing to trial tenant set, 4) Gradually migrate remaining traffic in 20% increments, with a rollback path to bypass the synchronizer if errors exceed thresholds.
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization logic, fuzz tests for label explosion, integration tests with a local Prometheus and OTLP generator, load tests using k6 and a synthetic tenant generator, and end-to-end parity tests against the existing pipeline. Include SLO regression checks and cost-attribution spot checks for accuracy within 2%.
